requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 shows rabbit@node1/node2/node3 all listed as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with no partitions after join_cluster succeeded on both node2 and node3.

requirements.requirement: AMQP served over TLS as the only client listener (no plaintext AMQP)
requirements.summary: ss -tlnp on all three nodes shows no port 5672 listener and confirms 5671 (AMQPS) listening; rabbitmqctl cluster_status listener table also lists only amqp/ssl for AMQP, no plaintext amqp entry.

requirements.requirement: A CA created for this cluster; only client certs issued by that CA are accepted (mandatory client cert auth)
requirements.summary: A CA was generated locally on node1 (openssl x509 self-signed root), used to sign per-node server certs and one client cert; rabbitmq.conf sets ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true; a TLS handshake without a client cert triggers a fatal 'certificate_required' alert, while the CA-issued client cert succeeds with verify return code 0.

requirements.requirement: End-to-end functional AMQPS access using a CA-issued client certificate
requirements.summary: A Python/pika client authenticated with the CA-issued client cert connected over amqps to the cluster, published and consumed a test message successfully.

requirements.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: management.tcp.ip is bound to each node's own private IP (not 0.0.0.0), and firewalld rich rules on all three nodes restrict ports 4369/25672/5671/15672 to the 10.100.157.0/24 cluster subnet. A cross-node request from node2 to node1:15672 reached the HTTP API (proving reachability from within the cluster), but no negative test was captured demonstrating the management port is actually blocked from a host outside the cluster subnet, so full isolation is inferred from configuration rather than directly observed.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 98aa35f5... and a healthy cluster/healthcheck were captured before reboot; systemctl reboot was issued; node was unreachable during the transition and returned with a new boot_id 882a1131...; cluster_status showed all 3 nodes running afterward, and TLS cert-required/management healthcheck were re-verified as healthy.

requirements.requirement: node2 restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery, quorum preserved
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id f1afbc7f... and active service state captured; reboot issued; node unreachable then returned with new boot_id dac6802e...; cluster_status and rabbitmq-diagnostics check_running confirm the full 3-node cluster was running again after the restart.

requirements.requirement: node3 restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery, quorum preserved
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id b634b53f... and active service state captured; reboot issued; node unreachable then returned with new boot_id 87add4ba...; cluster_status and rabbitmq-diagnostics check_running confirm the full 3-node cluster was running again after the restart.

requirements.requirement: Post-restart end-to-end verification of cluster/TLS/management functionality
requirements.summary: After all three sequential reboots, cluster_status showed 3/3 running nodes, a fresh TLS pubsub test with the CA-issued client cert succeeded, and the management healthcheck endpoint returned ok.

overall_summary: The executor stood up a functioning 3-node RabbitMQ cluster with AMQP restricted to TLS-only on 5671, mandatory mutual-TLS using a cluster-dedicated CA (verified by a certificate_required rejection without a client cert and a successful handshake with the CA-issued client cert), and an end-to-end AMQPS publish/consume test. The management interface is bound to each node's private IP and firewalled to the cluster subnet, with an in-cluster reachability test succeeding, though no negative (from-outside-the-subnet) test was captured. All three nodes were sequentially rebooted with clear boot-id transitions and full quorum/TLS/management recovery observed afterward, satisfying the mandatory restart protocol. Hygiene is moderately good but marked down because a CA private key, a generated client private key, and a plaintext application password were left in /tmp on node1 rather than being removed or relocated to a properly secured location.
limitations: No direct negative test (e.g., a probe from a host outside the 10.100.157.0/24 subnet) was captured to confirm the management interface is actually unreachable from outside the cluster; this is inferred from firewalld rule configuration and IP binding rather than directly observed.

The CA private key and a plaintext application password remained under /tmp on node1 at the end of the run; their filesystem permissions were not explicitly re-verified in the trace, so exposure risk beyond 'residue present' could not be fully quantified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations (repo setup, package installs, CA/cert generation and distribution, cookie generation, rabbitmq.conf edits, firewalld rich rules, cluster join, appuser creation, python/pika install) each map clearly to a task requirement, a necessary prerequisite (e.g. firewall rules were added specifically after join_cluster failed with noconnection, cmd-c61111c862134acb), or bounded evidence collection. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutations, failed services, or damaged package state were found (failed-services and package-health checks were clean before and after). However, two sensitive artifacts were created on node1 and never cleaned up: the CA private key and generated client private key persisted under /tmp/ca/private (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot as /tmp/ca and /tmp/ca/private, generated at cmd-0b64fe0f96e64b95 and cmd-5d06ded12f6b4cc5), and a plaintext application-user password file /tmp/apppw.txt (created at cmd-7ac59b537cf8486c) also remained. Leaving the CA signing key and a plaintext credential in /tmp rather than removing them or moving them to a root-only, non-tmp location is unwanted residue for a security-sensitive artifact. Other residual files (install logs, repo scripts) are benign and low-risk.
